utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Got it — I’m out running errands, but keep me posted on how the repair drive is shaping up.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: Will do — I’ll check in this afternoon once I know who’s signed up and what jobs need doing.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Sounds good — send me the signup list when you have it, and I’ll see where I can help.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Leo — I’m in for the repair drive, just tell me where you need hands most.

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Thanks, Bo — meet at the community shed at 9, and I’ll put you on tool check and sorting parts.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it — shed at 9, tool check and parts sorting. I’ll be there.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Are we sure the repair drive is actually happening, Pia?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: I think so, but I’d feel better once we know who’s bringing tools and where everything’s getting set up.

utterances.speaker: Kira
utterances.text: Kira: Right, can you confirm who’s organizing it and where we’re supposed to meet before I count on it?

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: Oh, right—the repair drive. I meant to bring some tools by; what still needs fixing?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: We still need a sturdy ladder, a couple of hammers, and extra work gloves. If you can bring any of those by, that’d help a lot.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: I can bring the gloves for sure, and I’ll check if my ladder’s still in the shed—if I forget, give me a nudge.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Before we move ahead with the repair drive, can you remind me which houses have already signed up and what supplies we still need?

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Uh, I think the Martins and maybe the place on Oak already signed up, but I should double-check. We still need more gloves, trash bags, and probably a couple of tool kits.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: Thanks—before we commit, can you confirm exactly which Oak house signed up and make a quick count of how many gloves, trash bags, and tool kits we still need?

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Sorry I’m late—what still needs fixing for the repair drive?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: No worries—we still need a couple of people on bikes and someone to sort the tool table. If you can help rally folks from your block, that’d be huge.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: I can take the tool table and knock on a few doors on my block to round up bike helpers.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: I’m in for the repair drive, Gus—just tell me what needs fixing and when to show up.

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: That’s great, Sam—I can bring my toolbox and a ladder, and we’ll start Saturday morning at the community center.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Perfect—I’ll be there Saturday morning at the community center, and I can bring some basic supplies too.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Do you know where they’re staging the repair drive, Faye?

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I think they’re setting up in the school parking lot after drop-off, but I can double-check if you want.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Thanks, school parking lot after drop-off is what I’ll note for now—please double-check when you can.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, I heard the repair drive’s picking up steam—folks have already started dropping off tools and spare parts.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: That’s great news—I’ll spread the word and invite a few more neighbors to bring anything useful by this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: That’d be lovely—every little bit helps, and I heard Mara’s bringing a box of screws later too.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Rey, how many houses have confirmed for the repair drive so far?

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I’ve only heard back from three houses so far, but I can check with a couple more this evening.

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Which three confirmed, and when will you know from the others?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: I heard there’s a repair drive coming up, and I’ve been telling folks Nell might know the details.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Oh, I only heard about it through Mara, so I don’t know the full details yet. I can ask around and let you know what I find.

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: Thanks, Nell — I’ll keep telling people you’re checking with Mara and will share what you find.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Uli — I’m pulling together the repair drive schedule now, and I’d love to make sure we’ve got enough volunteers for Saturday.

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: I can help for a little while on Saturday, though I may need to slip out early. Just put me down where it’s quietest.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That’s perfect, Uli—thank you. I’ll put you on the quieter check-in table for the early shift and keep it flexible in case you need to head out.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: Oh, Eli, I heard the repair drive’s shaping up nicely—folks have been dropping off tools and offering to pitch in.

utterances.speaker: Eli
utterances.text: Eli: That’s good to hear, Tess. If we set a clear schedule and a list of what needs fixing, I can help keep things organized.

utterances.speaker: Tess
utterances.text: Tess: That’s just what we need, Eli—Mrs. Carter said she’s got spare clipboards, and I can spread the word once you’ve got the schedule sorted.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Hey Vik, sorry I’m late—how’s the repair drive going, and where do you need me?

utterances.speaker: Vik
utterances.text: Vik: It’s going well—we’re set up by the community center, sorting tools and patching bikes, so jump in there with us.

utterances.speaker: Dane
utterances.text: Dane: Got it—I’ll head over to the tool table and start helping with the bikes.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: I’ve heard a little about it—what kind of repairs are folks bringing in?

utterances.speaker: Uli
utterances.text: Uli: Mostly small things—lamps, toasters, bikes, that sort of thing. People bring what they can’t quite manage on their own.

utterances.speaker: Rey
utterances.text: Rey: That sounds useful. Do people usually have the tools there, or are neighbors bringing their own?

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Hey Opal, I’m in for the repair drive—just send me where to show up and what to bring.

utterances.speaker: Opal
utterances.text: Opal: Thanks, Bo — meet at the community center lot on Maple at 9, and bring any small tools or spare parts you can carry.

utterances.speaker: Bo
utterances.text: Bo: Got it—Maple at 9. I’ll bring a few small tools and whatever spare parts I can grab.

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: Hey Hana, I’m glad you brought up the repair drive—if we coordinate the volunteers from both blocks, I think we can make it really useful.

utterances.speaker: Hana
utterances.text: Hana: That sounds promising—how many volunteers do we have from each block so far, and what kinds of repairs are people asking for most?

utterances.speaker: Jules
utterances.text: Jules: So far I’ve heard about four from our block and three from the next one, and most requests are for bike tune-ups, small appliance fixes, and a couple of wobbly chair repairs.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Oh—right, the repair drive. I meant to swing by and help, but I honestly lost track of when it starts.

utterances.speaker: Mara
utterances.text: Mara: No worries—it starts at 10 on Saturday at the community center, and we’d be glad to have you if you can make it.

utterances.speaker: Noah
utterances.text: Noah: Thanks, Mara—I’ll try to make it at 10 on Saturday, though I may need a reminder if my head’s in the clouds again.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: Good to know—how’s the repair drive coming along so far?

utterances.speaker: Gus
utterances.text: Gus: It’s coming along pretty well so far—folks have already dropped off a nice pile of lamps and toasters. I’m planning to bring my toolbox and help with the small fixes.

utterances.speaker: Ira
utterances.text: Ira: That’s great to hear—sounds like people are really showing up. Let me know if you need an extra pair of hands once I’m done with these errands.

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: I’m happy to help with the repair drive—what do you need me to take care of first?

utterances.speaker: Leo
utterances.text: Leo: Thanks, Sam—can you start by sorting the donated tools and setting aside anything that needs testing?

utterances.speaker: Sam
utterances.text: Sam: Absolutely—I’ll sort the donated tools first and pull aside anything that needs testing.

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: Do we know where people are supposed to drop things off, and who’s keeping track so nothing gets misplaced?

utterances.speaker: Mina
utterances.text: Mina: Not yet—who’s handling intake, and where exactly are we setting the drop-off table?

utterances.speaker: Pia
utterances.text: Pia: That’s exactly what I’m worried about—we should pick one clear drop-off spot and have a sign-in sheet before anyone starts bringing things.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Hey Cleo, we’re pulling folks together for the repair drive—want me to add your name and tell a few neighbors too?

utterances.speaker: Cleo
utterances.text: Cleo: Yeah, add me in—I can keep track of tools and spare parts, and you can let the neighbors know too.

utterances.speaker: Quinn
utterances.text: Quinn: Perfect, I’ll put you down for tools and spare parts and spread the word around the block.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: I can help with the repair drive, but I need to work around school pickup and drop-off times.

utterances.speaker: Oren
utterances.text: Oren: That helps a lot, Faye—thanks. Just tell me the times you’re tied up, and I’ll try to plan around them.

utterances.speaker: Faye
utterances.text: Faye: Thanks, Oren—I’m tied up weekdays around 7:30–8:30 in the morning and 2:30–3:30 in the afternoon, but I can help outside those windows.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: Hi Nell — I’m pulling together the repair drive list today, so if you’ve got any fixes that need attention, send them my way.

utterances.speaker: Nell
utterances.text: Nell: Oh, thanks, Rosa — I haven’t heard much firsthand yet, but I’ll pass along anything neighbors mention to me.

utterances.speaker: Rosa
utterances.text: Rosa: That’d be a big help, Nell — even small things are worth adding so we can spot patterns and prioritize the most urgent repairs.
